# cashew test fixtures

Three families: `real/`, `gen/` and `rust/`. Tests never invoke gpg or the network; they read these
committed bytes.

## `real/`

The deterministic, toolchain-pinned anchors: the actual kernel.org signer keys and a real release
signature, the ground truth the design rests on. `real/METADATA.toml` records the provenance and every
asserted fact.

- `greg-pruned.asc`, `sasha-pruned.asc`: Greg Kroah-Hartman and Sasha Levin public keys, exported
  through the §5.0 vendoring command (pruned, minimized, attribute-free, armored) from the
  authoritative `pgpkeys.git` at commit `ebb799f8`, toolchain gpg 2.4.9 / libgcrypt 1.12.2.
- `linux-6.6.30.tar.sign`: a real detached release signature, fetched from cdn.kernel.org. Its hashed
  issuer fingerprint is Greg's primary (the operative kernel.org shape).

A stale keyserver copy of Greg's key lacked his 2026-05 re-signatures and showed 2011 SHA-1 material,
and the R2 audit reproduced that trap. Key material therefore comes from `pgpkeys.git` only, never a
keyserver. To re-vendor:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/docs/kernel/pgpkeys.git   # then: git checkout ebb799f8
export GNUPGHOME=$(mktemp -d)
gpg --import pgpkeys/keys/38DBBDC86092693E.asc pgpkeys/keys/DEA66FF797772CDC.asc
# Greg (three live UIDs); Sasha (one live UID):
gpg --export-options export-minimal,no-export-attributes \
    --export-filter 'keep-uid=mbox=greg@kroah.com || mbox=gregkh@kernel.org || mbox=gregkh@linuxfoundation.org' \
    --export-filter 'drop-subkey=usage=e' --armor --export 647F28654894E3BD457199BE38DBBDC86092693E
gpg --export-options export-minimal,no-export-attributes \
    --export-filter 'keep-uid=mbox=sashal@kernel.org' \
    --export-filter 'drop-subkey=usage=e' --armor --export E27E5D8A3403A2EF66873BBCDEA66FF797772CDC
```

`export-minimal` semantics drift across gpg versions (dev.gnupg.org T7990), so the exports are
byte-reproducible within the pinned toolchain only; a toolchain bump is a re-derive and re-pin review
event.

## `gen/`

The throwaway differential corpus, generated by `gen.sh` (dev-host only, gpg 2.4.x). The keys are
randomly generated, so each regeneration produces a fresh corpus with new key fingerprints. Tests read
the per-run key fingerprints and the timestamps from `gen/MANIFEST.toml` and never hardcode them.
`--faked-system-time` stamps creation times from a fixed `gen_time` (the leading-zero sig at
`gen_time` plus its try count, recorded in `gen/MANIFEST.toml`), so the corpus is stable in shape and a single `fixture_now` sits after all of them. Tests evaluate the corpus at `fixture_now`
(`= METADATA.fixture_now`).

Files, covering both signing-key shapes:

- `key_a.asc`: RSA-4096 primary-signs `[SC]`, no signing subkey (the real kernel-dev shape).
- `key_b.asc`: RSA-4096 primary with a signing subkey (the chain shape; Component C / future signers).
- `key_c.asc`: a second `[SC]` signer (the "foreign / unpinned" negative).
- `key_d.asc`: adversarial, an expired signing subkey. It is a full export, not §5.0-minimal: on
  gpg 2.4.9 `export-minimal` strips expired subkeys (T7990), and the full export keeps the subkey so
  the parser and policy see it.
- `key_e.asc`: adversarial, a revoked signing subkey (0x28 revocation and binding preserved).
- `key_f.asc`: policy negative, a revoked primary (0x20).
- `key_g.asc`: policy negative, its only UID certification revoked (0x30 at the same faked second as
  the 0x13).
- `sig_<a|b>_<payload>_<sha256|sha512>.asc`: detached armored sigs over
  `payload_{empty,1b,1kib,5mib}.bin`, by key_a (primary) and key_b (subkey).
- `sig_a_1b_sha256_leadingzero.sig`: a sig whose integer `s` needs left-padding to the modulus width
  (bits ≤ 4088; pins the §6.4 left-pad-to-k requirement).
- `sig_a_1b_sha1_weak.asc`: a SHA-1 data sig (the `WeakHash(2)` negative).
- `sig_a_1b_sha256_expiring.asc`: a key_a sig that expires 3600 s after `gen_time`, expired at
  `fixture_now`.

No secret-key material is exported. The throwaway keys live only in `gen.sh`'s ephemeral,
loopback-pinentry `GNUPGHOME`, which is killed and removed on exit; no interactive prompt runs and no
operator keyring is touched.

## `rust/`

The `Keyring::load_pinned_bare` corpus, generated by `rust/gen.sh` (dev-host only, gpg 2.4.x, no
network). Its keys mirror the real Rust release key: an RSA-4096 `[SC]` primary with a SHA-1
self-cert, and the primary signs. A re-run produces a fresh corpus; tests bind to the committed bytes
and `rust/gen/MANIFEST.toml`.

- `gen/rust_key.asc`: the genuine pinned key, `[SC]` primary, SHA-1 self-cert, no subkey.
- `gen/rust_key_appended_subkey.asc`: the same primary with an appended signing subkey.
- `gen/foreign_key.asc`: a second, unpinned `[SC]` key (SHA-1 self-cert).
- `gen/manifest.bin`: a small manifest payload (opaque bytes at this layer).
- `gen/sig_primary_sha512.asc`: the manifest signed by `rust_key`'s primary, SHA-512 (the genuine
  data sig).
- `gen/sig_subkey_sha512.asc`: the manifest signed by the appended subkey, SHA-512. The bare path
  binds the primary only, so this sig must fail.
- `gen/sig_foreign_sha512.asc`: the manifest signed by `foreign_key`'s primary, SHA-512, from an
  unpinned key (`BadSignature`).
